# Kepler

> Kepler is GitKraken's Agentic Development Environment (ADE). It pulls every issue and pull request assigned to you into one place, then hands any of it to the coding agent you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Auggie, OpenCode, Grok Build, Pi, or Google Antigravity) with the context already attached.

Scope: 18 pages included. Excluded (3): environment-and-setup.md, kepler-New-Page-Template.md, workflow-views.md.

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started with Kepler](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/kepler-getting-started/): Install Kepler, connect an agent and your trackers, and put an agent on real work in a few minutes.

## Core Concepts

- [The Kepler Interface](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/kepler-interface/): Kepler opens on your work - every issue and pull request assigned to you, alongside the tasks you already have running. Learn how to read it, work several items side by side, and start work from it.
- [Arranging Your Work](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/arranging-your-work/): One interface means you shape it rather than switch away from it. Choose an arrangement, group, sort and filter the list, save a combination as a named view, set a task's progress, and archive in bulk.
- [Actions](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/actions/): Actions are editable named prompts you fire at a task, issue, or pull request. Learn the four built-in Actions, how to change them, and how to write your own.
- [Tasks and Resources](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/tasks-and-resources/): A Task is the unit of work in Kepler. Learn what a Task holds, how worktrees work, and how everything attached to a Task reaches your agents.
- [The Task View](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/task-view/): Open a Task to see its resources, agent sessions, changes, and files side by side. Learn the header, the rail, columns and free-form tabs, the file viewer, and how to start sessions and terminals.
- [The Agent Graph](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-graph/): A live graph of everything your agents are doing - every task, session, turn, tool call, subagent, and file, drawn as it happens.

## Working in Kepler

- [Create a Task](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/create-task/): Start a Task from an issue, a pull request, or nothing at all, with the repository, branch, and context already attached.
- [Agent Sessions](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-sessions/): An agent session is one running conversation with a coding agent inside a Task. Learn how to start one, pick the agent and account, queue prompts, answer the agent's questions, track usage limits, and keep sessions running through restarts.
- [Review Changes](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/review-changes/): An agent finished. Read the diff in the Changes overlay, comment on it, stage and commit, update the branch from its base, and hand the rest to AI Sync or Compose.
- [Voice Input](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/voice-input/): Dictate to an agent instead of typing. Voice input transcribes on your device with Whisper, works push-to-talk or hands-free, and is available in remote windows.

## Integrations

- [Agent Integrations](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-integrations/): Kepler runs the coding agent you already have. Connect Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Auggie, OpenCode, Grok Build, Pi, or Google Antigravity, or point Kepler at your own ACP server.
- [MCP Servers](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/mcp-servers/): See the MCP servers each agent loads, turn a server or a single tool on or off per repository or for every repository, add and remove servers, and sign in to the ones that need it, from inside Kepler.
- [Issue Tracker Integrations](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations/): Connect your issue trackers to Kepler, cloud or self-hosted, so the issues you're working on land in one list, with everything an agent needs already attached.
- [Pull Request Integrations](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/pull-request-integrations/): Connect your Git hosts to Kepler, cloud or self-hosted, so the pull requests you authored and the ones waiting on your review land in one list, already matched to the worktrees they belong to.

## Configuration

- [Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings/): A reference for every setting in Kepler across the eleven Settings sub-pages, plus folder locations, branch prefixes, the Variables menu, per-repository commands, MCP server defaults, and the keyboard shortcut list.
- [Remote Environments](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/remote-environments/): Run your agents on another machine over SSH or in WSL, switch environments from the title bar, manage hosts in Settings, forward an SSH host's ports to this computer, and open this Kepler from another device with Remote Access.

## Release Notes

- [Kepler 0.x](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/release-notes-current/): View the latest features, improvements, and fixes shipping in the current version of Kepler.
